newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Dec 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Dec 3.

text.p: Finance Minister Bill Birch carefully set the scene for increased government spending as he issued the latest Treasury forecasts on Monday. The forecasts are slightly less optimistic than figures issued before the election, but still show continuing economic growth and steadily increasing government surpluses. Birch pointed to the projected surpluses as evidence that government spending could increase. Labour finance spokesman Michael Cullen said the slight deterioration in the forecasts showed "the effects of the high-flying Kiwi dollar are coming home to roost". His first priority if he became finance
minister would be to lower the exchange rate. Page 1.

NZ First leader Winston Peters said on Monday night he still hoped the makeup of the next government would be known when parliament sat next Tuesday. But Labour leader Helen Clark said she was relaxed about the issue. Peters said on television: "I am hoping, probably about 95 percent, that we are going to make it well before that date." Parliament is expected to convene next Tuesday, but does not have to sit till December 13. Page 1.

One in five farms and orchards may have to be sold in the next 12 months as eroding export returns cripple the rural industry, an ACT NZ taskforce report says. The report criticises the government's handling of the economy, saying the export sector is suffering because excessive government spending is driving inflation and has led to New Zealand having the highest real interest rates in the world. Page 2.

Prime Minister Jim Bolger was preparing to "sell out" National list MP Jim Gerard and back Attorney-General Paul East as parliament's speaker in order the help secure a coalition deal with NZ First, Labour MP Mike Moore said on Monday. Page 2.

Allegations of a price-fixing conspiracy have been levelled by Clear Communications at Telecom, its main shareholders, giant American media groups Time Warner and TCI, and Sky Television. Clear has gone to the High Court seeking declarations that they breached the Commerce Act. It also wants injunctions against Telecom, and damages and costs. Page 14.

The government has downgraded its forecast budget surpluses for the next four years, but said it expected growth in the domestic economy to counter pressure on exporters. The December Economic and Fiscal Update, which updated the pre-election fiscal update in September, showed an operating budget surplus of $2.493 billion was now expected in the current 1996-97 year, down from the $2.866 billion forecast in September. Hellaby Holdings has taken an option to buy 51 percent of New Zealand's largest footwear retailer, Hannahs, and confirmed it is to buy swimsuit maker Expozay. Chairman Bill Falconer said Hellaby had been granted an option to buy the Hannahs stake next year in return for funding it is to provide. "The company now seeks to embark on a major refurbishing and reimaging programme to retain and build its market leadership," he said. Page 14.

The sharemarket started the week with a roar on Monday in a belated reaction to steep falls in interest rates in the past week. The NZSE 40 capital index was up 19.47 points on a high Monday turnover of $79 million. Telcom was the star of the day, accounting for more than $43 million of the turnover, including a huge crossing of 3.75 million shares at $7.45. Page 14.
